meta.title: Forge CLI — Crucible
meta.description: Forge — AI environment sync tool becoming the Harness Compiler. Distribute shared skills across Claude Code, Cursor, Windsurf, Copilot, and Cline.

hero.headline: One source of truth for every AI tool.
hero.subheadline: Today, Forge is a dead-simple sync engine — point it at a repo, it distributes skills to Claude Code, Cursor, Windsurf, Copilot, and Cline in the right format. But that's just the foundation. Forge is becoming the Harness Compiler — same CLI, new brain: dependency graphs, tree-shaking, token budgets, per-agent optimization. Think Vite, but for AI agents.

setup.heading: Two minutes to set up. Zero maintenance.

global.title: Global setup (once per machine)
global.description: Run forge init --global and point it at your team's shared resource repo. The wizard detects your AI tools and writes the config. That's it — every new project you open gets synced automatically.

project.title: Per-project setup (once per repo)
project.description: Need project-specific skills? Run forge init inside the repo. Same wizard, same simplicity. Once configured, forget about it — Forge keeps everything in sync.

setup.footer: No YAML to hand-edit. No complex configs to learn. The wizard handles everything.

source.heading: Best paired with an AI Resources Platform
source.description: Forge pulls from any git repo. But for the best experience, we recommend using a structured {link} as your source — it gives you convention-over-configuration, versioned resources, automated testing, and a clear lifecycle from idea to delivery.
source.note: Forge works with any git source. The resources platform just makes it better.

items.title: Set & Forget
items.description: Run the wizard once. It detects your AI tools, adds a git source, enables auto-sync scheduling. Never think about it again.

items.title: Easy Updates
items.description: Check status, spot drift, add a second source, sync everything. No YAML editing, no guessing — the wizard handles it.

items.title: Power User
items.description: Fine-grained source control with subdirectories, include/exclude filters, merge strategies, dry-run preview, and health dashboard.

items.desc: Interactive wizard — detects AI tools, configures sources, writes config.
Fetches from all sources, resolves targets, places files for each assistant.
Shows drift between last sync and current filesystem state.
SLI dashboard — sync frequency, drift count, source reachability.
Interactive config editor with section-based menu.
Shows configured sources with type, synced file counts.
Remove a source with optional cleanup of synced files.
Edit existing source configuration with pre-filled values.
Shows telemetry status, config, and what's collected.
Removes .crucible directory, scheduler, and all synced files.

assistants.heading: 5 assistants. One config.
assistants.footer: Adding a new assistant = one file. Zero command handler changes.

items.title: Multi-source
items.description: Parallel fetching via Promise.allSettled. Failed sources don't block others.

items.title: Conflict resolution
items.description: Source + local conflict strategies: last-wins, first-wins, or error.

items.title: Backup
items.description: When remote-wins overwrites local changes, .bak copies are created automatically.

items.title: SHA-256 detection
items.description: No unnecessary rewrites. Only writes when content actually changed.

items.title: Dry-run
items.description: Preview all changes without writing. See what would happen before it does.

items.title: Rollback
items.description: On mutation failure, already-written files are rolled back. No partial state.

items.title: Health dashboard
items.description: SLI metrics: sync frequency, drift count, source reachability, active assistants.

canonical.title: Canonical
canonical.description: Flat files organized as skills/, rules/, workflows/ — distributed and transformed per assistant.

preStructured.title: Pre-structured
preStructured.description: Contains assistant-specific directories (.claude/, .cursor/, etc.) — copied as-is without transforms.

hybrid.title: Hybrid
hybrid.description: Mix of both — canonical files transformed and distributed; pre-structured files copied directly. Auto-detected by default.

compiler.heading: Coming next: Forge becomes the Harness Compiler
compiler.description: Same forge CLI you already use — but under the hood, a full compiler pipeline. Other tools install files. Forge will compile your AI environment.

items.title: Dependency graph
items.description: Skills declare dependencies via frontmatter. Forge resolves the full DAG, detects cycles, and orders output correctly.

items.title: Tree-shaking
items.description: Java project? Python skills are automatically excluded. Forge detects project context from marker files and prunes irrelevant skills.

items.title: Per-agent optimization
items.description: Claude Code gets priority-ordered individual files. Cursor gets merged rule files. Each agent gets skills in its optimal format.

items.title: Token budgeting
items.description: Set per-agent context limits. When total exceeds budget, lowest-priority skills are dropped first. Dependencies are always protected.

items.title: Build manifest
items.description: Every compile emits a manifest — skill IDs, versions, hashes, agent targets, token estimates. This is Ember's data source.

items.title: Smithery integration
items.description: Pull skills from agentskills.io as a source. Their 25k-star skill ecosystem becomes compiler input.

cta.heading: Ready to get started?
cta.description: Install Forge, run forge init, and sync your first config in under 2 minutes. The compiler features are coming in v0.7.
